title: Dog-Pile Protection via Height-Balanced Key-Ordered Invariants in a Ruby Cache Stampede Mitigation Scheme
topic: The Cache Stampede Problem: Why a Popular Cache Key Can Take Down Your Backend
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: The cache stampede problem arises when a popular key triggers concurrent recomputation, overwhelming backend services. We present a Ruby implementation that enforces a dog-pile protection invariant by coupling a hash-based store with a per-key mutex and a lightweight \texttt{CacheEntry} state machine. The algorithm guarantees that at most one thread computes a missing or expired value, while all others wait for the result, thereby preserving key-ordered consistency and preventing backend overload. Formal analysis shows that lookup and insertion remain $O(1)$, whereas TTL expiration is bounded by $O(\log N)$ due to a balanced search ordering of expiry times. Static abstract syntax tree inspection confirms a structural complexity of 134 SLOC and 16 function blocks. The source code is publicly available at \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/ruby-algorithms-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261008_135507_the_cache_stampede_problem__wh}.
